errands.name: a warding on the walls
errands.text: pale sigils are chalked on every gate, and the townsfolk sleep easier.

errands.name: rain on the fields
errands.text: a soft rain falls on the fields for three days, and the granaries fill.

errands.name: a scrying of the wilds
errands.text: the mages spend a night over their mirrors and send the council word of places nobody had heard of.

errands.name: a cure for the lanes
errands.text: a mage walks the poor lanes with a censer, and the coughing stops.

plots.name: the Long Night at the Pens
plots.pitch: someone's sons and daughters are in those pens. Get in, get them out, and do not wake the place.

plots.name: the Vault Job
plots.pitch: a crew, a plan, a vault no one has ever opened, and one night to do it.

plots.name: Bring Them Home
plots.pitch: they marched out and never came back. Somebody has to bring their bones to their mothers.

plots.name: the Quiet Graves
plots.pitch: the old village has gone silent, and the dead no longer stay where they were put. Find out why.

plots.name: the Fallen Champion
plots.pitch: once someone's hero, now someone's nightmare. Talk them down or cut them down.

plots.name: the Hunt for the Great Beast
plots.pitch: something huge has been taking cattle, then shepherds. Track it to its den and end it.

plots.name: Hold the Line
plots.pitch: a handful of blades against a horde, before it falls on the farms. Every song worth singing starts this way.

plots.name: Words Before Swords
plots.pitch: send the silver tongues first. Blood is for when talk fails.

ways.line: {text}: {name} the {class} casts a spell of flight and floats the party over it, no roll needed.
{text}: {name} the {class} asks the stone and the wind to let them by, and they do.
{text}: {name} the {class} sends an unseen servant ahead, and it sets the trap off for them.
{text}: {name} the {class} reads the answer in a divination and walks straight to it.
{text}: {name} the {class} weaves a charm into a few kind words, and the path opens.
{name} the {class} charms the guards at {text} into waving the party through without a blow.

heist._doc: Quiet jobs (terms with heist: fetch, rescue). Before each room the party's quietest tries to slip past (DC sneakDc + perTier a tier); a failure fights the room and raises the alarm, and at alarmMax the place wakes (wake more foes in every room after) and nobody slips past anything. The hoard on a fetch sits in a vault of layers[tier-1] locks, wards and hidden catches (kinds, in turn) at layerDc + perTier a tier, sharing the same alarm: at alarmMax inside the vault they run with bolted of the gold and no treasure.

terms.name: Slay
terms.text: Kill what lives there and bring back the hoard. The place stays empty longest.

terms.name: Drive off
terms.text: Break them and let them run. Half the fighting and a third of the hoard, and something moves back in sooner.

terms.name: Talk down
terms.text: Send heroes with silver tongues to talk them into leaving. No blood if it works; a fight if it doesn't. Only for foes clever enough to bargain.

terms.name: Rescue
terms.text: Slip in far enough to cut the captives loose, then get them home. Every room they cannot sneak past is a fight and raises the alarm. The place itself is left standing.

terms.name: Fetch
terms.verb: steal the best of the hoard from
terms.text: Get in quietly, past the vault's locks and wards, take the best thing in the hoard for the town, get out. Every slip raises the alarm, and if it gets to the top inside the vault they run with half the gold and no treasure.

terms.name: Recover
terms.verb: bring home the fallen company lost at
terms.text: Fight in to where a company of ours fell, and bring home their bones and the gear they carried. The place itself is left standing.
